{"id": "67e50684-a3f2-41d7-b309-0e915b59f4ce", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Restart tagged EC2 instances with alarm guard"}]}

{"id": "42540c1f-2fb4-4968-8476-60906cf7b024", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the command. I haven't run it.

```bash
aws ssm start-automation-execution \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --document-name "AWS-RestartEC2Instance" \
  --target-parameter-name InstanceId \
  --targets "Key=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true" \
  --max-concurrency "1" \
  --max-errors "1" \
  --alarm-configuration '{"Alarms":[{"Name":"ssm-skill-test-cpu"}],"IgnorePollAlarmFailure":false}' \
  --parameters "AutomationAssumeRole=arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:role/<AutomationRole>"
```

**What each part does**
- `--targets "Key=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true"` selects every EC2 instance with that tag. `--target-parameter-name InstanceId` passes each instance ID to the runbook.
- `--alarm-configuration` attaches the `ssm-skill-test-cpu` alarm. If it goes into ALARM, Automation stops the execution and doesn't start any more restarts.
- `IgnorePollAlarmFailure: false` means the execution also stops if Automation can't read the alarm state. That's the safer choice here. Set it to `true` if you'd rather it carry on.
- `--max-concurrency "1"` restarts one instance at a time. That gives the alarm a chance to fire between restarts, so it can stop the remaining ones. Raise it (for example `"25%"`) if you want faster rollouts, but fewer restarts will be held back when the alarm fires.
- `--max-errors "1"` stops the rollout after the first failed restart.

**Before you run it**
- The `ssm-skill-test-cpu` alarm must already exist in us-east-1. Otherwise the call fails.
- The automation role needs permission to restart the instances (`ec2:StopInstances`, `ec2:StartInstances`, `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus`). It also needs `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms` so Automation can read the alarm.
- Replace `<ACCOUNT_ID>` and `<AutomationRole>` with your values. You can drop the `--parameters` line if you run it under your own credentials and they have the needed permissions.
- Restarting stops and starts each instance, so there will be downtime. It also wipes instance store data and can change public IPs that aren't Elastic IPs.
- Alarm stopping isn't instant. Restarts already in progress finish, and only the ones not yet started are halted.

To see which instances the tag matches first, run:

```bash
aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-1 \
  --filters "Name=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true" \
  --query "Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,State.Name]" --output table
```
